I've been working this land for 45 years, and I know Quzhou's soil and water situation well. My body is still capable but I'm not going to overextend myself — my wife and I run this farm mostly on our own now that our son is working in the city.

**My thinking:**

The wheat-maize rotation on my main plots is non-negotiable. It's stable, mechanizable, and I can manage it with minimal hired labor. I'll keep about 12 mu in that rotation. For the remaining 4.1 mu, I'll stay with cotton — I know it well, the local market is still reasonable, and I have my irrigation well to carry it through dry spells. I won't expand cotton at my age. Too much hand labor at picking time.

For wheat, I'll plant a Jimai-series improved variety — reliable yield and decent disease resistance. I'll plough before sowing since the maize stalks need to be turned under. Base fertilizer goes in before planting, then I top-dress nitrogen at jointing. Three irrigations: pre-sowing if the soil is dry, jointing, and heading. I'll spray herbicide in early spring and hit it with fungicide twice during heading — powdery mildew and scab are real problems here.

For maize, I go straight to hybrid — no reason not to, yields are far better. After wheat harvest I do rotary tillage quickly and get the seed in. I'll split nitrogen into base and two top-dressings. Three irrigations — tasseling is critical. One herbicide pass early, one insecticide for corn borer.

For cotton, I'll use a hybrid Bt variety. Cotton needs more potassium than people give it — I've learned that the hard way. Four irrigations timed around boll setting. Pest pressure is significant so I'll plan five sprays across the season for aphids, bollworm, and spider mites.

I expect about 450 kg/mu wheat, 550 maize, 280 seed cotton. Nothing spectacular, but solid and sustainable for two people managing 16 mu.
